questions.question: What STIs does the 7-in-1 kit test for?
questions.answer:
The kit contains 5 rapid tests that check for 7 infections between them. Every test gives its own result, so you’ll know exactly what was and wasn’t detected.

HIV

HIV attacks the immune system and can cause no symptoms for years. Treatment is free on the NHS and highly effective. Learn about the symptoms and stages of HIV.

Syphilis

Syphilis is a bacterial STI that often starts with a painless sore that’s easy to miss. It’s curable with antibiotics. Learn about the four stages of syphilis.

Chlamydia and gonorrhoea

These are two of the most common STIs in the UK, and most people with chlamydia have no symptoms. Both are treated with antibiotics. Learn about chlamydia and gonorrhoea symptoms.

Genital herpes (HSV-2)

Herpes is a virus passed on through skin-to-skin contact. Most people with it have no symptoms. There’s no cure, but outbreaks can be managed. Learn about genital herpes symptoms and outbreaks.

Hepatitis B and C

These viruses infect the liver and can spread through blood, and hepatitis B through sex. Many people have no symptoms. Hepatitis C is usually curable with tablets. Find out more on our hepatitis B and C test page.

questions.question: Can you have an STI without knowing?
questions.answer: Yes, and it’s very common. Most people with chlamydia have no symptoms. HIV and hepatitis can cause no symptoms for years. Up to 90 in 100 people with herpes don’t notice any signs. Syphilis can start with a painless sore that heals by itself. Testing is the only way to know, even if you feel completely well.

questions.question: Who is the 7-in-1 kit for?
questions.answer:
You don’t need symptoms to test. The 7-in-1 kit is a good choice if:

  • You want a full sexual health check in one go
  • You’ve had sex without a condom, or with a new partner
  • You have more than one partner and want to test regularly
  • A partner has told you they have an STI, and you’re not sure which tests you need
  • You’re starting a new relationship and want peace of mind
  • You’d prefer a private home test to a clinic visit

Need help now? If you have symptoms or a partner has tested positive, contact a sexual health clinic now.

Possible HIV exposure in the last 72 hours? Contact a sexual health clinic or A&E as soon as possible and ask about PEP, medicine that can help prevent HIV after exposure. Don’t wait for a test result.

aside.heading: Why choose a full STI test kit?
aside.text: If you’ve been exposed to one STI, you may have been exposed to others. Many STIs have no symptoms, and the ones that do often look alike. Testing for one infection can leave the rest unchecked. A full STI test kit gives you the complete picture in one go.

accordions.heading: What does the 7-in-1 bundle test for?
accordions.content:
Chlamydia and gonorrhoea are bacterial infections that often cause no symptoms. Both can be cured with antibiotics.

HIV is a virus that affects the immune system. It cannot be cured, but treatment is highly effective.

Syphilis is a bacterial infection that can cause a painless sore or rash, or no symptoms at all. It can be cured with antibiotics.

Genital herpes (HSV-2) is a virus that can cause genital blisters or sores. There is no cure, but outbreaks can be treated with antiviral medicine.

Hepatitis B and C are viruses that affect the liver. Many adults recover from a new hepatitis B infection naturally, while hepatitis C can usually be cured with antiviral tablets.

windows.heading: How soon after sex can I take a full STI test?
windows.subheading:
You can test straight away, but testing too early can give a negative result even if you have an infection. An early negative may need repeating: chlamydia and gonorrhoea at 2 weeks, syphilis and hepatitis B at 12 weeks, HIV at 90 days and hepatitis C at six months after your last possible exposure. There isn’t a reliable number of days or weeks when the herpes IgM test becomes conclusive.

results.heading: How to read your 7-in-1 STI test results

groups.intro:
Every test has a C (control) line and a T (test) line. The C line shows the test worked. A T line, even a faint one, means something was detected. Two of the tests have two windows, so you get a separate result for each infection.

TestWindow(s)NegativePositive
HIVOneC line onlyC and T lines
SyphilisOneC line onlyC and T lines
Chlamydia & gonorrhoeaCt (chlamydia) and Ng (gonorrhoea)C line only in bothC and T lines in the Ct and/or Ng window
Herpes (HSV-2)OneC line onlyC and T lines
Hepatitis B & CHBsAg (hepatitis B) and HCV (hepatitis C)C line only in bothC and T lines in the HBsAg and/or HCV window

Invalid: No C line in a window means that test hasn’t worked, even if a T line shows. Contact us and we’ll help.

notes.title: What if a result is positive?
notes.text:
Don’t panic. Every infection in this kit can be treated or managed, and NHS sexual health services are free and confidential. Contact a sexual health clinic or your GP for a confirmation test and treatment. Your recent partners may need testing too.

A few results need extra care:

  • Herpes (HSV-2): a positive can’t show when you were infected, and IgM can return during a repeat outbreak.
  • Hepatitis C: antibodies can stay after the infection has cleared, so a positive may mean a past infection.
  • Syphilis: antibodies can stay after treatment, so tell the clinic if you’ve had syphilis before.

notes.title: Good to know
notes.text: These tests are designed for screening and don’t replace advice from a doctor or nurse. For ages 16 and over.

questions.question: What STIs does the 7-in-1 kit test for?
questions.answer: It tests for 7 infections: HIV (types 1 and 2), syphilis, chlamydia, gonorrhoea, genital herpes (HSV-2), hepatitis B and hepatitis C. There are 5 tests in the box, and each gives its own result.

questions.question: How long do the results take?
questions.answer: Each test gives a result in around 15 minutes, read at home. The herpes test can be read up to 30 minutes. Doing all 5 tests usually fits into a single sitting.

questions.question: Do I need to send a sample to a lab?
questions.answer: No. These are rapid tests you read yourself at home. There’s nothing to post and no waiting days for results.

questions.question: How accurate is the 7-in-1 STI test kit?
questions.answer: When used correctly, each test is a reliable screening test. In clinical evaluations, 99.81% of syphilis results matched a lab test. Testing too soon after exposure can affect results, and any positive result should be confirmed by a clinic or GP.

questions.question: Is the 7-in-1 kit cheaper than buying tests separately?
questions.answer: Yes. The same 5 tests cost £98.75 bought separately. The 7-in-1 kit is £64.95, so you save £33.80. If you plan to retest, the 2-kit Test + retest pack is £116.92, saving a further 10%.

questions.question: What’s the difference between the 7-in-1 kit and the Core 4 bundle?
questions.answer: The Core 4 bundle tests for chlamydia, gonorrhoea, HIV and syphilis for £44.95. The 7-in-1 kit adds genital herpes, hepatitis B and hepatitis C for £64.95. Choose the 7-in-1 for the most complete check.

questions.question: Can men and women use the 7-in-1 kit?
questions.answer: Yes. The kit is for anyone aged 16 and over. The swab test works with a vaginal swab or a swab from the urethra (the tube you pee from).

questions.question: Does it test for throat or anal infections?
questions.answer: No. The chlamydia and gonorrhoea test uses a genital swab only. If you’ve had oral or anal sex, ask a sexual health clinic about throat or rectal testing.

questions.question: Does it test for HSV-1?
questions.answer: No. The herpes test checks for HSV-2 only. HSV-1 is the cold sore virus, which can also cause genital herpes through oral sex. A clinic can swab any sores to find out which type it is.

questions.question: How soon after sex can I use the kit?
questions.answer: You can test straight away, but each infection takes a different time to show up. If you test early and get negative results, retest at 2 weeks, 90 days and 6 months. See the window periods in “When to test”.

questions.question: What if one of my results is positive?
questions.answer: Contact a sexual health clinic or your GP for a confirmation test and treatment. Every infection in the kit can be treated or managed, and NHS sexual health services are free and confidential. Your recent partners may need testing too.

questions.question: What does a negative result mean?
questions.answer: It means that infection wasn’t detected. If you tested soon after possible exposure, you may have tested too early, so retest once its window period has passed. If you have symptoms, speak to a sexual health clinic.

questions.question: Can I use the kit while pregnant?
questions.answer: The swab test is not recommended if you are pregnant. If you’re pregnant and concerned about STIs, speak to your midwife, GP or a sexual health clinic. HIV, syphilis and hepatitis B testing is routinely offered during pregnancy through the NHS, and they can advise on testing for the other infections.

questions.question: Which STI tests do I need?
questions.answer: If you’re not sure, a full STI test is the simplest choice. Many STIs have no symptoms and they often look alike, so testing for one can miss another. The 7-in-1 kit covers the most common STIs and blood-borne infections in one order. Read more about how STI testing works.

questions.question: How often should I get an STI test?
questions.answer: Test after sex without a condom or with a new partner, and regularly if you have more than one partner. Testing before sex with a new partner is also a good idea. A sexual health clinic can advise how often is right for you.

questions.question: Can you have an STI without symptoms?
questions.answer: Yes. Most people with chlamydia have no symptoms, and HIV, hepatitis and herpes can cause no symptoms for years. You can still pass an infection on, so testing is the only way to know.

questions.question: What are the most common STIs in the UK?
questions.answer: Chlamydia is the most commonly diagnosed STI in England, with 151,163 diagnoses in 2025. There were also 63,943 gonorrhoea diagnoses, 28,779 first episodes of genital herpes and 8,262 syphilis diagnoses.

questions.question: Are STIs curable?
questions.answer: Many are. Chlamydia, gonorrhoea and syphilis are cured with antibiotics, and hepatitis C is usually cured with tablets. Most adults clear hepatitis B on their own. HIV and herpes can’t be cured, but treatment works very well and lets people live long, healthy lives.

questions.question: What’s the difference between an STI and an STD?
questions.answer: They mean the same thing. STI stands for sexually transmitted infection, and STD stands for sexually transmitted disease. STI is the term used most in the UK, because you can have an infection without any signs of disease.

questions.question: Can I get a free STI test on the NHS?
questions.answer: Yes. NHS sexual health clinics offer free, confidential testing, and some areas offer free postal kits that you send to a lab. Many people choose a rapid home test for 7 results in around 15 minutes, with no appointment and no sample to post.

questions.question: Will anyone know what I ordered?
questions.answer: No. Your kit arrives in plain, discreet packaging with nothing on the outside to reveal what’s inside. Your bank statement won’t show “Test Discreet” or the name of the test.

questions.answer: We ship within 1 working day, with discreet delivery across the UK.
